claims.claim: All 35 passages the reporters drew from the AI-suspected France guidebook scored 100 on Originality.ai's AI detector.
claims.source: Seth Kugel and Stephen Hiltner, The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: All 35 passages scored a perfect 100
claims.page: section following the annotated Amazon listing
claims.modelEra: unidentified generative text tool of the GPT-3.5/GPT-4 era, measured by the NYT in August 2023; register measured = printed travel-guidebook place description

claims.claim: Of 190 paragraphs the reporters tested from 64 further comparably formatted guidebooks, 166 scored 100 and only 12 scored under 75.
claims.source: Seth Kugel and Stephen Hiltner, The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: 166 scored 100, and only 12 scored under 75
claims.page: section following the annotated Amazon listing
claims.modelEra: unidentified generative text tools of the GPT-3.5/GPT-4 era, measured by the NYT in August 2023; register measured = printed travel-guidebook place description

claims.claim: Passages from the human travel brands Rick Steves, Fodor's, Frommer's and Lonely Planet scored nearly all under 10 on the same detector, the control against which the guidebook scores were read.
claims.source: Seth Kugel and Stephen Hiltner, The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: nearly all under 10
claims.page: section following the annotated Amazon listing
claims.modelEra: detector run August 2023 on human-written guidebooks in print at that date; register measured = printed travel-guidebook place description

claims.claim: Originality.ai claimed the detector version used mistakes human text for AI on just under 1.6 percent of tests.
claims.source: Originality.ai's claim as reported by The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: just under 1.6 percent of tests
claims.page: section following the annotated Amazon listing
claims.modelEra: Originality.ai detector version supplied to the NYT, August 2023; register measured = mixed web and book prose

claims.claim: The reader who bought the AI-suspected France guidebook was disappointed by its vague descriptions, in the reporters' paraphrase of her.
claims.source: Amy Kolsky, paraphrased by Seth Kugel and Stephen Hiltner, The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: vague descriptions, repetitive text and lack of itineraries
claims.modelEra: guidebook printed on demand and bought March 2023, generative tool unidentified; register measured = travel-guidebook place description

claims.claim: The same reader found the guidebook's text repetitive, in the reporters' paraphrase of her.
claims.source: Amy Kolsky, paraphrased by Seth Kugel and Stephen Hiltner, The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: vague descriptions, repetitive text and lack of itineraries
claims.modelEra: guidebook printed on demand and bought March 2023, generative tool unidentified; register measured = travel-guidebook place description

claims.claim: The reader's own account of the guidebook was that it read as though facts had been copied off the internet and pasted in.
claims.source: Amy Kolsky quoted in The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: copied a whole bunch of information from Wikipedia and just pasted
claims.modelEra: guidebook bought March 2023, generative tool unidentified; register measured = travel-guidebook place description

claims.claim: More than ten guidebooks published under one author name shared a cookie-cutter design and similar promotional language, the reporters found.
claims.source: Seth Kugel and Stephen Hiltner, The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: same cookie-cutter design and use similar promotional language
claims.page: opening section, on the Stuart Hartley titles
claims.modelEra: Amazon self-published guidebooks appearing in the months before August 2023; register measured = travel-guidebook place description

claims.feature: other: generic superlative in the evaluative close
claims.claim: A guidebook on Lviv closed by inviting the reader to an unforgettable adventure in one of Eastern Europe's most captivating destinations, a passage the reporters quote as characteristic of the books.
claims.source: Text of an AI-suspected Lviv guidebook (May 2023), quoted by The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: an unforgettable adventure in one of Eastern Europe’s most captivating destinations
claims.modelEra: guidebook published May 2023, generative tool unidentified; register measured = travel-guidebook place description

claims.feature: other: material omission in place description
claims.claim: That Lviv guidebook, published in May 2023, fails to mention the war.
claims.source: Seth Kugel and Stephen Hiltner, The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: also fails to mention the war
claims.modelEra: guidebook published May 2023, generative tool unidentified; register measured = travel-guidebook place description

claims.feature: other: material omission in place description
claims.claim: A Moscow guidebook published in July 2023 makes no mention of Russia's ongoing war with Ukraine.
claims.source: Seth Kugel and Stephen Hiltner, The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: makes no mention of Russia’s ongoing war with Ukraine
claims.modelEra: guidebook published July 2023, generative tool unidentified; register measured = travel-guidebook place description

claims.claim: Rick Steves said that writing a good guidebook requires being in the field.
claims.source: Rick Steves quoted in The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: you’ve got to be there in the field to write one
claims.page: section headed 'You've got to be there in the field'
claims.modelEra: spoken to the NYT in July or early August 2023 about generative AI guidebooks; register discussed = travel-guidebook place description

claims.claim: Frommer's editorial director Pauline Frommer characterised the imitation guidebooks as sweeping the internet and putting random crap down.
claims.source: Pauline Frommer quoted in The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: sweep the internet and put random crap down
claims.page: section 'Amazon, A.I. and trusted travel brands'
claims.modelEra: spoken to the NYT in mid-2023; register discussed = travel-guidebook place description

claims.claim: Darby Rollins, founder of a company that helps businesses use generative AI, judged the guidebooks very basic.
claims.source: Darby Rollins quoted in The New York Times, 5 August 2023
claims.quote: very basic
claims.page: section headed 'You've got to be there in the field'
claims.modelEra: spoken to the NYT in mid-2023 about 2023-era guidebook output; register measured = travel-guidebook place description

claims.feature: other: refusal to let AI write history and place sections
claims.claim: A Wikivoyage administrator said in the AI-policy discussion that history, culture and climate are sections he absolutely does not want an AI to handle.
claims.source: User:LPfi, Wikivoyage talk:AI guidelines, 16 May 2026
claims.quote: History, culture, climate etc. are things I absolutely don't want
claims.modelEra: unnamed LLMs as of May 2026; register discussed = travel-gazetteer background sections (history, culture, climate)

claims.feature: other: plausible completeness that omits the important
claims.claim: The same editor argued that a background section which looks complete but misses important points is as bad as a factual error about a train service.
claims.source: User:LPfi, Wikivoyage talk:AI guidelines, 16 May 2026
claims.quote: as bad as telling about a train that doesn't run
claims.modelEra: unnamed LLMs as of May 2026; register discussed = travel-gazetteer background sections

claims.claim: The one Wikivoyage user known to have posted AI-generated discussion comments was disruptive mostly through flowery language, according to the editor who dealt with it.
claims.source: User:LPfi, Wikivoyage talk:AI guidelines, 16 May 2026
claims.quote: highly disruptive, mostly by using flowery language
claims.modelEra: unnamed chatbot, observed on Wikivoyage before May 2026; register measured = wiki discussion prose

claims.claim: An experienced Wikimedia policy editor recalled a study finding that people who do not use AI have about a fifty-fifty chance of guessing whether a sample of text was AI-generated.
claims.source: User:WhatamIdoing, Wikivoyage talk:AI guidelines, 4 September 2026
claims.quote: 50–50 chance of guessing whether a piece of sample
claims.modelEra: an unnamed study recalled from memory in September 2026; register measured = unspecified sample text. Confidence medium: the editor cites no study by name.

claims.claim: The same editor found a passage on English Wikipedia he suspected of being AI-generated and discovered from the page history that it had been written 22 years earlier.
claims.source: User:WhatamIdoing, Wikivoyage talk:AI guidelines, 4 September 2026
claims.quote: it was written 22 years ago
claims.modelEra: observation made around September 2026 about human text from about 2004; register measured = encyclopedic prose

claims.feature: other: human prose preferred for style
claims.claim: The Wikivoyage draft guideline opens by telling contributors that prose is nearly always better written by them, for style.
claims.source: User:LPfi/AI guidelines, English Wikivoyage draft marked experimental, revision of September 2026
claims.quote: The prose is nearly always better written by you, for style
claims.modelEra: generative AI generally, as assessed by Wikivoyage editors in mid-2026; register measured = travel-gazetteer article prose. Note: a userspace draft, not adopted policy.

claims.claim: The same draft explains AI invention as the model asserting a particular beach resort has a restaurant because many resorts do, that is, substituting the typical for the particular.
claims.source: User:LPfi/AI guidelines, English Wikivoyage draft marked experimental, revision of September 2026
claims.quote: has a restaurant because many do
claims.modelEra: generative AI tools as of mid-2026; register measured = travel-gazetteer listings and place description. This is a MECHANISM claim, not a tell.

claims.claim: The same draft tells editors to avoid converting an existing article into an obvious AI voice.
claims.source: User:LPfi/AI guidelines, English Wikivoyage draft marked experimental, revision of September 2026
claims.quote: avoid converting an article into an obvious AI voice
claims.modelEra: generative AI tools as of mid-2026; register measured = travel-gazetteer article prose

claims.claim: The same draft characterises what a large language model returns as some average or mishmash of its inputs.
claims.source: User:LPfi/AI guidelines, English Wikivoyage draft marked experimental, revision of September 2026
claims.quote: some average or mishmash of the inputs
claims.modelEra: large language models of the mid-2020s, as characterised in mid-2026; register measured = travel-gazetteer article prose. MECHANISM claim.

claims.claim: The same draft bars AI from talk-page posts and instructs editors not to use the style AI chatbots tend to use.
claims.source: User:LPfi/AI guidelines, English Wikivoyage draft marked experimental, revision of September 2026
claims.quote: do not use the style AI chatbots tend to use
claims.modelEra: AI chatbots as of mid-2026; register measured = wiki discussion prose

claims.feature: other: generic epithet in place description
claims.claim: A travel writer following a ChatGPT itinerary quotes the model's own place words as charming backstreets and authentic souvenir shops, flagging them as the robot's phrasing.
claims.source: Thom Brown, Intrepid Times, 2 January 2026
claims.quote: “charming backstreets” and “authentic souvenir shops” (the robot’s words
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT, itinerary generated for a Tallinn trip in December 2025 and published January 2026; register measured = travel itinerary and place description

claims.claim: The dishes ChatGPT recommended at the restaurant it named did not exist on that restaurant's menu.
claims.source: Thom Brown, Intrepid Times, 2 January 2026
claims.quote: the food suggestions offered by my artificial master do not exist
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT, December 2025 Tallinn trip; register measured = travel recommendation

claims.claim: The oddly specific cocktail ChatGPT ordered the writer to request, which he expected to be fabricated, turned out to exist.
claims.source: Thom Brown, Intrepid Times, 2 January 2026
claims.quote: It’s real,” I beam
claims.page: night of the ChatGPT day, at the bar
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT, December 2025 Tallinn trip; register measured = travel recommendation. Kept as counter-evidence against a blanket invention claim.

claims.claim: The writer reports that the model, kept to one small district, seemed to run out of ideas and told him to watch locals buying coffee.
claims.source: Thom Brown, Intrepid Times, 2 January 2026
claims.quote: it seems to have run out of ideas
claims.page: comparison section after the Lonely Planet day
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT, December 2025 Tallinn trip; register measured = travel itinerary and place description

claims.claim: The human guidebook supplied an institutional particular about a named cathedral that the model's itinerary did not, that it was set to transform into a planetarium in the 1960s.
claims.source: Thom Brown, Intrepid Times, 2 January 2026, on Lonely Planet's Estonia, Latvia & Lithuania
claims.quote: set to transform into a planetarium in the 1960s
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT compared against a Lonely Planet print guide, December 2025; register measured = place and institution description

claims.claim: The writer's summary judgement is that he prefers a human-written guide to the slop AI puts between practical advice.
claims.source: Thom Brown, Intrepid Times, 2 January 2026
claims.quote: the sprinkles of slop that AI tends to vomit between practical
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT, December 2025 Tallinn trip; register measured = travel writing

claims.feature: other: first-hand observation as the boundary
claims.claim: Lonely Planet's editorial policy states that AI does not and cannot do the on-the-ground reporting work the brand rests on.
claims.source: Lonely Planet, Editorial Policy on AI (vendor page, fetched 6 September 2026)
claims.quote: AI does not and cannot do that work
claims.modelEra: AI tools generally as of the policy's publication, undated but live September 2026; register discussed = guidebook and destination writing

claims.feature: other: first-hand observation as the boundary
claims.claim: The same policy states the publisher does not use AI to create original editorial reporting, recommendations, reviews or destination expertise.
claims.source: Lonely Planet, Editorial Policy on AI (vendor page, fetched 6 September 2026)
claims.quote: We do not use AI to create original editorial reporting
claims.modelEra: AI tools generally as of the policy's publication, live September 2026; register discussed = guidebook and destination writing

claims.claim: The same policy discloses that AI does write the reader-facing quick-summary blocks at the top of certain destination articles, condensing human reporting within editorially designed templates.
claims.source: Lonely Planet, Editorial Policy on AI (vendor page, fetched 6 September 2026)
claims.quote: Quick-summary blocks at the top of certain destination articles
claims.page: section 'Where AI shows up for readers'
claims.modelEra: AI summarisation tools in use at Lonely Planet as of September 2026; register measured = destination-article summary

claims.claim: A local-history author reports that ChatGPT, asked about Eleanor Roosevelt, called Theodore Roosevelt her husband.
claims.source: Michael Burgess quoted by Nitish Pahwa, Slate, November 2025
claims.quote: Eleanor and her husband Theodore Roosevelt
claims.page: section on the History Press authors
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT, as tried by the author and reported in November 2025; register measured = local and regional history

claims.source: Michael Burgess quoted by Nitish Pahwa, Slate, November 2025
claims.quote: not going to go and get microfilm
claims.page: section on the History Press authors
claims.modelEra: AI generally, as assessed by the author in 2025; register discussed = local history
